interactions.summary: Jiang answers the evolution-versus-design objection by contrasting a detached architect God with Dante's always-present God, whose light actively shines through creatures inside the cosmic body.
A student compresses Jiang's distinction into a rough game-developer versus game-master metaphor, which Jiang accepts as serviceable but limited.

A student tests the shining-light idea with a mirror image, and Jiang pulls the class back to Beatrice's preferred metaphor by saying God is the brain and humans remain oriented toward God within the body.

The class begins Canto 3, and Jiang turns the invocation of sun, Apollo, God, inspiration, and Beatrice into a paradox about one love appearing through different forms; a student answers with Blake's language of emanations.

speaker_notes.note: The student analogy is clear, but the ASR duplicates the word 'game' and clips the ending; the conceptual contrast is still stable enough to use.
The middle of this span is garbled, but Jiang's main point remains that the mirror image is less precise than the body metaphor with God as brain.
These spans mix poem reading, Jiang prompts, and a student interpretation. They should be treated as a guided interpretive exchange rather than pure Jiang monologue.

claims.claim: Jiang distinguishes a detached architect God who designs the rules and stops caring from Dante's God, who remains with human beings and shows approval by shining light through them.
claims.temporal_scope: Jiang interpretive contrast stated on 2026-06-15 while answering a student's Darwinism question.

claims.claim: The student reframes Jiang's contrast as the difference between a game developer who only builds the system and a game master who actively plays inside it.
Jiang says the evolutionary picture under discussion treats the universe as independent of God, whereas Beatrice's account says God is always present through differentiated shining.
Jiang reasserts the cosmic-body frame by saying God is the brain rather than treating humans as separate mirrors merely reflecting an external light.
claims.temporal_scope: Idea clarified in classroom exchange on 2026-06-15.

claims.claim: Jiang treats the poem's opening sun as simultaneously Apollo, God, inspiration, and Beatrice, forcing the class to reconcile multiple sacred names inside one passage.
claims.temporal_scope: Jiang interpretive setup stated on 2026-06-15 as the class opens Canto 3.

claims.claim: A student borrows Blake's language of emanations to say Beatrice can stand on behalf of Apollo and God as a more concrete representative presence.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang turns the student's Darwinism challenge into a clean theological split between a God who built the game and left and a God who is still inside the world shining through it.
signature_moments.source_phrase: god is an architect who designed the rules of the universe and no longer cares
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It sharpens the lecture's earlier design-versus-emergence contrast into a memorable distinction between absentee architecture and living presence.

signature_moments.moment: The metaphysical distinction suddenly becomes legible in gamer language.
signature_moments.source_phrase: the difference between a game developer and a game master
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This is the quickest lay translation of Jiang's abstract point about divine absence versus participation.

signature_moments.moment: The class resolves the Apollo-God-Beatrice paradox through the idea of emanations, letting one force appear in several concrete forms.
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It previews a recurring Jiang move: apparent multiplicity becomes intelligible once the class sees different figures as manifestations of one source.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: Jiang's label for a deistic conception in which God designs the rules of the universe and then does not remain actively involved.
Borrowed from Blake to describe figures such as Beatrice as representative manifestations of a deeper divine force.
Jiang's compressed version of the universe-as-body model, where God functions as the coordinating intelligence within the cosmic whole.

chronology_notes.note: This packet continues the same June 15 lecture by moving from the Darwinism objection into Canto 3's paradox of divine manifestations; it does not introduce a new dated position outside the source session.

uncertainty_notes.note: Part of Jiang's reply is garbled, so the packet preserves only the stable conceptual point that he prefers the body-and-brain metaphor over the mirror image.
